title: Add check_site_with_retry helper
description: Wraps check_site with a retry loop: on each attempt it opens a brand-new browser context/page (a stale page is often the actual cause of a timeout, not the site), runs check_site, and accepts the result as soon as it comes back with no error entries. If check_site raises instead of returning an error result, that's caught and turned into the same shape of single-entry error result the existing code already produces, so it retries the same way. Every attempt's context is closed in a finally block. If every attempt (the original try plus max_retries retries) still errors, the last attempt's results/error are returned rather than raising, matching check_site's own existing error-shape data instead of introducing a new one to main().
acceptance_criteria: check_site_with_retry(browser, site, headless, max_retries=SITE_MAX_RETRIES) is defined at module level
Each attempt calls browser.new_context() and context.new_page() fresh, and closes that context in a finally block before the next attempt or return
It returns immediately once an attempt's results contain no entry with a truthy 'error' key

An unhandled exception from check_site is caught, logged with print(f"  Failed: {e}"), and converted into a one-entry error result with the same fields check_site's own timeout branch uses (site, job_title, status, date_applied, error)
Between attempts (never after the final one) it prints a retry message naming the site and the attempt number, then sleeps via time.sleep before trying again
If every attempt is exhausted without a clean result, the last attempt's results are returned (never raises)
